messages.author: a3527f6489543e9b
messages.subject: Imputation of non-wear time
parts:
Dear GGIR group

I wonder if anyone has an answer to my question related to the imputation of non-wear time in GGIR. In one of our research projects, participants were asked to record the times when they removed the device and the associated reasons. We are interested in knowing whether it is possible to feed this information into GGIR by specifying the time segment(s) where we want GGIR-based imputation to be performed and those where we want them to be imputed by a specific intensity category.

For example, if we know that the device was removed from 9:00-9:30 for running, can we set this 30 minutes as MVPA? For other time segments detected as non-wear by the GGIR algorithm but not reported by participants in their log diary, we would still want the auto-imputation to be done. I know there is an option of using the TimeSegments2ZeroFile, but my understanding is that it only works with relabelling the non-wear/invalid segments as zero movement (e.g., when the participants did not wear the devices for sleep). 

Thank you.

Best regards,
John.

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Imputation of non-wear time
parts:
Hi Vincent et al

I have a further question about the data imputation procedure. Based on the explanations provided on this page, the non-wear periods or segments with clipping problems will not be imputed if do.impute is set as FALSE, and that the recorded values are kept as they are and not imputed or omitted. Does this mean that the identified non-wear periods (eg. 10-10.30am) will still be included in the analysis even though they have been flagged as non-wear and treated as invalid? And will the initial metric value (or zero) be included in the data file for further processing?

Thank you.

Best regards,
John.

messages.author: 017566be30afa7f3
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Imputation of non-wear time
parts:
Hi John,

Except for the imputation, GGIR behaves the exactly same between both settings. 
You either trust the data without imputation or with imputation. Leaving out the data is not an option as that effectively means imputing by the average of the remaining valid data, which I have tried to avoid.

Best wishes,

Vincent
